headline: Bought more Search cheaply; the leads came back worth far less
commentary:
Yesterday broke a 14-day run of profitable days: **NP -$1,163 at -2.87% NM**, against +$3,089 and 7.34% last Thursday. The RateSpecial top-up hasn't landed yet, but on 17/09 it was only $266 — it won't turn this day positive, so treat the loss as real.

Search did the damage. We actually bought better and bigger: CPC $12.19 vs $14.10, clicks 2,783 vs 2,238, impression share 12.84% vs 9.99%, leads 1,472 vs 1,217. What we didn't get was value — **Search EPL $22.83 vs $28.22 last Thursday and $25.89 MTD**, which flipped Search from +$1,676 to -$2,667. Google's own conversion column looks unlanded (19 on payday_alternative), so I'm reading leads off our side only.

The softness wasn't confined to Search. Every Google ping tree came in under its 7-day average — Test Ping Tree $17.16 vs $23.44, Direct (Inc ZP) $19.47 vs $21.52, Direct Lenders $15.55 vs $19.91 — and Bing EPL fell to $9.92 from $13.36. That pattern points at buyer-side pricing on the day rather than one bad campaign. The 05:00–12:00 window was the worst of it: roughly $2,800 of clicks returning about $780, a ~$2,000 hole in a shoulder period we usually tolerate.

Context matters: blended EPL $13.05 sits at the very bottom of the last eight Thursdays (mean $14.61, min $13.08), so this is an outlier day, not a drift — one day doesn't make a trend. MTD NM is 9.81% versus 12.4% for the same days last month, with **Search CPC at $12.90 MTD against $9.06** — auction inflation remains the structural squeeze. Small bright spot: PMAX turned $185 profit on EPL $11.32, though on 184 leads that's lumpiness, not a new baseline.
watch: Search EPL today — a second day under about $24 against $25.89 MTD makes this a lead-value trend, not noise.
personal spend jumped to $1,508 from $681 after the 22/09 SA removal and tROAS lift to 137%, and scavenger went $113 to $601; check both are selling before they scale further.
Bing EPL $9.92 vs $11.45 MTD on $3,758 spend — if it repeats today, trim the daily allocation.
